about.title: Clovis Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You are on the ground in a grocery aisle off Shaw Avenue, or in a parking lot along Herndon Avenue, embarrassed and trying to stand up before anyone notices. Later, when the wrist will not bear weight or the knee swells overnight, the questions start. In Clovis, as elsewhere in Fresno County, the property owner is not automatically responsible because you were hurt on their premises. California law asks whether the owner knew about the hazard, or reasonably should have known, and then failed to repair it or warn people about it. That is where evidence matters most: the puddle, the buckled mat, the unlit stairwell, the missing handrail. Photographs taken that day, names of anyone who saw it happen, and a prompt written request that the business preserve its surveillance footage can shape the entire claim. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Clovis residents, at no cost, with an independent premises liability attorney who can evaluate what happened and what comes next.

whyChoose.title: Why Clovis Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice is the heart of the case
items.desc: A California owner is responsible only if they knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. The attorneys in our network know how to look for inspection logs, prior complaints, and maintenance records that speak to that question.

items.title: Video disappears quickly
items.desc: Many Clovis retailers and apartment communities overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out early is often the difference between a documented fall and a disputed one.

items.title: Deadlines and shared fault both matter
items.desc: Most California premises claims must be filed within two years, and the window is much shorter when a public entity owns the property. Under pure comparative fault you can still recover even if you were partly to blame, with your share reduced accordingly.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk or in a park owned by the City of Clovis. Is the process different?
items.answer: Yes, and the difference is significant. Claims against a California public entity, including a city or Fresno County, generally require a written government claim within six months of the injury rather than the two-year period that applies to private owners. Missing that step can end the claim before it starts, so it is worth speaking with an attorney soon after a fall on public property.

items.question: The store manager said I should have been watching where I was going. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not by itself. California uses pure comparative fault, which means a jury or adjuster assigns percentages of responsibility rather than an all-or-nothing answer. If you are found partly at fault, your recovery is reduced by that percentage, but it is not eliminated. Whether the hazard was visible, marked, or long-standing all factor into that analysis.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall in Clovis?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if the pain seems manageable, because records created early carry weight later. Photograph the hazard and the surrounding area if you can, write down what you were doing and what you noticed, and collect contact information from anyone who saw it. Then ask the business in writing to preserve any camera footage from that day. An attorney in the LawProactive network can send that request for you if you reach out promptly.
